Scheduled AI work shouldn’t require a server you keep babysitting.

Aeon is a fork-and-configure autonomous agent framework for operators who want to run AI skills on a schedule from GitHub Actions.

It helps you turn recurring work into configured skill runs by enabling skills and schedules in `aeon.yml`, while each run starts as a fresh, headless agent invocation.

Key features:

• Skill configuration – enable individual skills and set their schedules in `aeon.yml`
• GitHub Actions runtime – runs skills on GitHub Actions without a long-lived process
• Fresh-run model – each skill run starts as a new headless invocation
• Git-backed memory – state persists in the repository and `memory/` directory between runs
• Health and repair loop – health skills score runs, while repair skills can create fixes through PRs

It’s open-source (MIT license).

Link in the reply 👇

quoted_tweet.text:
there’s something quite awkward about all the personal agents in the current hype cycle

muse, grok bot, instinct, dots, and whatever google, anthropic will come up with

none of them is “mine”

i’d be trusting a vendor for some of the most sensitive data about me and bet on them handling it with extreme responsibility. what if they have a data leakage incident? what if they hired a wrong employee? what if they simply break bad?

i’d also be betting on their model. right now i’ve set up a lot of my stuff in grok bot, but what if their model falls behind? what if another model becomes 10x better on pure intelligence? then i’ll either miss out on a better assistant, or have to bite the bullet and do a full migration

i’d also have to bet on their product. they may not build the features i want. they may not allow me to customize enough. and one day my assistant may show me ads

that feels like way too much betting than what i’d be comfortable with, if i truly want literally everything in my life to go through and be taken care of by an assistant

with all that considered, i’m more bullish on open source personal agents that run on people’s own computers. but i think these open source projects have to break out of the assumption that their users are developers and they can just throw a repo at them and ask them to launch a terminal

a well polished, fool proof, community maintained, vendor agnostic, free personal agent that everyone can run by themselves without locking into a SaaS - that’s what i think many people will need

retweeted_tweet.text:
hello, superintelligence.

the interesting question isn’t how smart the next model gets.

it’s what happens when that intelligence can keep working after you close the laptop. give it a computer 

that’s what we’re building at @aeonframework.

an open-source agent that lives in a repo you own and keeps running through github actions. its memory is in git, its skills are markdown, and it can use tools, run on a schedule, create new skills, repair failing ones, improve itself by this and leave every change behind for you to inspect.

you can give it a job and let it keep going on research, code, review, deploy, security and whatever else you need it to handle.

and there’s real proof behind it.

the vuln-scanner has already secured 103 open-source repos, fixing 138 findings across 4 critical, 81 high, 43 medium and 10 low severity findings.

those repos represent 4.8M github stars.

NVIDIA, Google, Microsoft, Alibaba, Tencent, xAI, Vercel, Cloudflare and many more.

agents have been finding real vulnerabilities, opening fixes, getting them merged and running the whole loop while their owners are offline.

engineers at OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceX, GitHub and others are already using $AEON.

this is where i think AI/Si is heading: give increasingly capable models the tools, memory, permissions and autonomy to take on real work and keep going without someone sitting in the chat.

that’s what we’re building with @aeonframework.

https://t.co/rAf1kWfQYI
